newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end higher on bargain hunting.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end higher on bargain hunting.

text.p: Malaysian shares closed higher, rebounding from Monday's fall on bargain hunting coupled with a 78-point rally on Wall Street overnight.
Dealers said the improved market sentiment led to increased trading volume.

"Volume is back to more than 500 million. I believe the heavy delivery situation is about over," said an institutional dealer. Heavy share deliveries from last week had pressured the market on Monday.
The benchmark Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks closed up 12.85 points or 1.04 percent at 1,250.33.
The small-capitalised Second Board index was up 9.48 points or 1.45 percent to 662.50.

Stocks in the DRB-Hicom group of companies were mixed after falling on their requotation on Monday. Analysts said there were still concerns surrounding the group's future following the death of former chairman Yahaya Ahmad on March 3.
Proton rose 30 cents to 15.90 ringgit and Edaran Otomobil Nasional was up 70 cents to 25.50, while Hicom fell 20 cents to 6.60 ringgit and Diversified Resources was down 15 cents to 8.80.
